headline: Boston Dynamics has explained why the new hand for its Atlas humanoid robot has four fingers instead of five, and says it is not yet fitted across its robot fleet.
score_reason: Kept at 5: a trade-press interview with new design detail on a hand first shown about 1 Oct 2026; company statements only, with no outside test.
importance_line: Factories that may one day use the Atlas humanoid get a hand designed to be simpler, sturdier and cheaper to build, but the evidence is the company's own account and the hand is not yet on the whole fleet.
summary: The Robot Report reports, in an interview with Alberto Rodriguez, director of robot behavior for Atlas at Boston Dynamics, that the company's new four-fingered hand for its Atlas humanoid robot, which drops the pinky and uses a smaller gripper, has 13 degrees of freedom (13 independent joint movements) and is built from 13 identical sealed actuators with no fragile cables crossing joints. Rodriguez said the hand was designed to be simulated accurately so robots can learn to use it by trial and error in simulation, that it can still handle objects over 100 lb, and that it has been used extensively at headquarters but not yet fitted to the whole fleet.
notes: The hand itself was shown about 1 Oct 2026 (date from search listings); today's piece is a follow-up interview. Everything is Boston Dynamics's own account.
